lesson: Today we work on one technique, scale, scale means the poem moves between something very small and something very large within a few lines. Watch how this poem does it. It starts small with a skin of cold coffee filmed across the bottom. Then it stays small, each blade holding its own small weight of frost. Then it goes wide. The maples have started their slow turn toward giving up green. A single blade of grass, then whole trees, then the season changing. This works in a plain way. When you jump from something tiny to something big, the listener feels the size of both at once. The small thing feels close, the big thing feels wide. You notice both because they sit right next to each other. Try this, put one tiny detail and one large thing in two lines that touch with nothing between them. The second time through hold the frost on one blade against the turning maples and let so up land.
